subject: Biotechnology
title: The Four Colors of Biotech
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Four Colors of Biotech.

hook.text: Biotechnology is so vast that scientists color-code it — red, green, white, and blue.

buildup.text: Red biotech is medical — drugs, gene therapy, diagnostics. Green is agricultural — crops and livestock.

discovery.text: White biotech is industrial — enzymes, biofuels, biomaterials. Blue is marine — ocean organisms.

twist.text: The boundaries blur — a marine enzyme used in medicine is both blue and red biotech simultaneously.

climax.text: New colors keep appearing — gold for bioinformatics, grey for environmental applications.

punchline.text: Biotech has more colors than the rainbow — and growing.

quiz.question: What does 'red biotechnology' refer to?
options: Medical applications like drugs and gene therapy

details.summary: Biotechnology is classified into four color-coded sectors: red for medical biotech, green for agricultural biotech, white for industrial biotech, and blue for marine biotech. Each color represents a major application area with distinct products, challenges, and regulatory frameworks.
details.whyItMatters: The color classification helps organize the vast biotechnology landscape into understandable categories. It reveals how the same core technologies in genetics and microbiology serve radically different industries from healthcare to ocean resource
takeaways: Red biotech covers pharmaceuticals, diagnostics, and gene therapy
Green biotech encompasses GMO crops, biopesticides, and plant genetics
White biotech includes industrial enzymes, biofuels, and bio-based materials

faq.question: What does each color of biotechnology represent?
faq.answer: Red is medical: drugs, vaccines, diagnostics. Green is agricultural: GMO crops, biopesticides. White is industrial: biofuels, enzymes, biomaterials. Blue is marine: products from ocean organisms. Some add grey for environmental biotech and yellow for food and nutrition biotech.

faq.question: Which color of biotechnology is the largest by revenue?
faq.answer: Red biotech dominates by far, representing over 60 percent of total biotechnology revenue. Biopharmaceuticals alone generate hundreds of billions annually. Green biotech is second through GMO seed sales, followed by white biotech with industrial enzymes and biofuels.
